knowledge:
- key_parameters: eSet=An ExpressionSet object containing the normalized expression matrix and phenotypic metadata ;; f=The column name in the phenotypic metadata representing the grouping factor to analyze (must be an R factor) ;; GO_genes=A data frame mapping gene feature identifiers to GO identifiers ;; all_GO=A data frame containing GO term descriptions ;; all_genes=A data frame containing gene descriptions ;; N=The number of permutations to perform in pValue_GO (at least 1,000 is recommended for robust p-values) ;; subset=A named list specifying subsets of samples to analyze or plot on-the-fly
- alternatives: Random Forest (default method in GO_analyse) vs ANOVA F-score (specified via the method argument, more stable but less flexible for non-linear interactions) ;; Online Ensembl queries (automatic when custom annotations are omitted) vs Local custom annotations (highly preferred for speed, reproducibility, and offline capability)
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have a normalized gene expression dataset (microarray or RNA-seq) and a multifactorial experimental design, and you want to identify, rank, and visualize functional gene ontology groups or individual genes that drive the classification of your experimental groups.
- pitfalls: The grouping factor column specified by f must be explicitly formatted as an R factor, otherwise the analysis may fail or yield incorrect results ;; GO terms with very few associated genes are inherently biased to rank higher; calculate permutation-based p-values using pValue_GO and filter results using subset_scores (setting a minimum total gene count) to control this bias ;; Running GO_analyse without local annotations is slow as it queries Ensembl servers and is subject to web-service availability ;; Subsetting an ExpressionSet manually can leave unused factor levels in the metadata, which causes Random Forest to crash; use droplevels() or subEset() to clean up factor levels.

workflows.name: supervised_go_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform supervised classification of samples to rank GO terms and genes, calculate permutation-based p-values, filter results, and visualize expression profiles and sample clustering.
input: user_expression_data.RData (An ExpressionSet object containing normalized expression data and phenotypic metadata)
custom_annotations.RData (Optional local annotation data frames: GO_genes, all_GO, and all_genes)
workflows.stages:
1. Load the package and dataset.
2. Ensure the grouping factor is formatted as an R factor.
3. Run the supervised classification analysis using GO_analyse.
4. Compute permutation-based p-values for GO terms using pValue_GO.
5. Filter the results by ontology namespace, minimum gene count, and p-value using subset_scores.
6. Visualize sample clustering and gene expression using heatmap_GO or cluster_GO.
7. Extract gene details for a specific GO term using table_genes or list_genes.
8. Plot individual gene expression profiles across experimental factors using expression_plot or expression_profiles.
workflows.code:
library(GOexpress) # load the GOexpress package
data(AlvMac) # import the training dataset
is.factor(AlvMac$Treatment) # assertion test
AlvMac$Treatment # visual inspection
AlvMac$Treatment <- factor(AlvMac$Treatment)
set.seed(4543) # set random seed for reproducibility
AlvMac_results <- GO_analyse(
    eSet = AlvMac, f = "Treatment",
    GO_genes=AlvMac_GOgenes, all_GO=AlvMac_allGO, all_genes=AlvMac_allgenes)
AlvMac_results.pVal = pValue_GO(result=AlvMac_results, N=100)
BP.5 <- subset_scores(
    result = AlvMac_results.pVal,
    namespace = "biological_process",
    total = 5, # requires 5 or more associated genes
    p.val=0.05)
heatmap_GO(
    go_id = "GO:0034142", result = BP.5, eSet=AlvMac, cexRow=0.4,
    cexCol=1, cex.main=1, main.Lsplit=30)
cluster_GO(
    go_id = "GO:0034142", result = BP.5, eSet=AlvMac,
    cex.main=1, cex=0.6, main.Lsplit=30,
    subset=list(Time=c("24H", "48H")), f="Group")
table_genes(go_id = "GO:0034142", result = BP.5)[,c(1:3)]
list_genes(go_id = "GO:0034142", result = BP.5)
expression_plot(
    gene_id = "ENSBTAG00000047107", result = BP.5, eSet=AlvMac,
    x_var = "Timepoint", title.size=1.5,
    legend.title.size=10, legend.text.size=10, legend.key.size=15)
AlvMac$Animal.Treatment <- paste(AlvMac$Animal, AlvMac$Treatment, sep="_")
expression_profiles(
    gene_id = "ENSBTAG00000047107", result = AlvMac_results,
    eSet=AlvMac, x_var = "Timepoint", line.size=1,
    seriesF="Animal.Treatment", linetypeF="Animal",
    legend.title.size=10, legend.text.size=10,
    legend.key.size=15)
plot_design(
    go_id = "GO:0034134", result = BP.5, eSet=AlvMac,
    ask = FALSE, factors = c("Animal", "Treatment", "Time", "Group"),
    main.Lsplit=30)

workflows.name: custom_annotation_generation
workflows.intent: Download and prepare custom Ensembl annotations via biomaRt for offline, fast, and reproducible GOexpress analyses.
input: ensembl_host_metadata (The Ensembl archive host URL and dataset name corresponding to the target species)
workflows.stages:
1. Connect to the Ensembl BioMart database using biomaRt.
2. Download gene annotations (IDs, symbols, descriptions).
3. Download GO term annotations (IDs, names, namespaces).
4. Download the mapping between gene IDs and GO IDs.
5. Clean and format the downloaded data frames.
6. Save the custom annotations to local R data files (.rda) for offline use in GO_analyse.
workflows.code:
library(biomaRt)
listMarts(host='feb2014.archive.ensembl.org')
ensembl75 = useMart(
    host='feb2014.archive.ensembl.org',
    biomart='ENSEMBL_MART_ENSEMBL', dataset='btaurus_gene_ensembl')
allgenes.Ensembl = getBM(
    attributes=c('ensembl_gene_id', 'external_gene_id', 'description'),
    mart=ensembl75)
colnames(allgenes.Ensembl)[1] = 'gene_id'
allGO.Ensembl = getBM(
    attributes=c('go_id', 'name_1006', 'namespace_1003'),
    mart=ensembl75)
GOgenes.Ensembl = getBM(
    attributes=c('ensembl_gene_id', 'go_id'),
    mart=ensembl75)
colnames(GOgenes.Ensembl)[1] = 'gene_id'
GOgenes.Ensembl = GOgenes.Ensembl[GOgenes.Ensembl$go_id != '', ]
GOgenes.Ensembl = GOgenes.Ensembl[GOgenes.Ensembl$gene_id != '', ]
save(GOgenes.Ensembl, file='GOgenes.Ensembl75.rda')
save(allGO.Ensembl, file='allGO.Ensembl75.rda')
save(allgenes.Ensembl, file='allgenes.Ensembl75.rda')
GO_analyse(
    eSet=AlvMac, f='Treatment',
    GO_genes=GOgenes.Ensembl,
    all_GO=allGO.Ensembl,
    all_genes=allgenes.Ensembl)
